title: Noah's Flood
lead: The great flood of Genesis 6–9, God's judgment on a violent world and his rescue of Noah's family and the animals in the ark. Later Scripture uses it as a pattern of judgment and salvation (Isaiah 54:9; Matthew 24:37–39; 1 Peter 3:20–21; 2 Peter 3:5–7). Mesopotamian literature tells related flood stories.

sections.b: Isaiah 54:9–10 compares God's oath after the flood with his promise of lasting peace to Israel. Ezekiel names Noah with Daniel and Job as models of righteousness (Ezekiel 14:14, 20). Jesus uses "the days of Noah" as a warning that judgment comes suddenly (Matthew 24:37–39; Luke 17:26–27). Hebrews 11:7 praises Noah's faith, 1 Peter 3:20–21 links the ark to baptism, and 2 Peter 2:5 and 3:5–7 compare the flood with the coming judgment by fire. Whether the flood was worldwide or regional, and how it relates to Atrahasis and Gilgamesh, is discussed in the notes on Genesis 7:19 and 8:8.
